arxiv-2105-02762.title: Flex Net Sim: A Lightly Manual
arxiv-2105-02762.creator: Felipe Falcón, Gonzalo España, Danilo Bórquez-Paredes
arxiv-2105-02762.description: Abstract A common problem in elastic optical networks is to study the behavior of different resources allocation algorithms, such as signal modulation formats or quality of service, in optical networks in dynamic scenarios where connections are assigned and released following different traffic profiles. To achieve this, one of the busiest tools is simulators.

arxiv-2111-03582.title: Application of TMD parton showers obtained with the Parton Branching approach to Drell Yan + jets production
arxiv-2111-03582.creator: H. Yang
arxiv-2111-03582.description: Abstract Calculations of Drell-Yan (DY) production at next-to-leading (NLO) order have been combined with Transverse Momentum Dependent (TMD) distributions obtained with the Parton Branching (PB). The predictions show a remarkable agreement with DY measurement from E605 experiment, consistent with previous results we obtained for R209, PHENIX, CMS and ATLAS experiments.

arxiv-2210-02406.title: Decomposed Prompting : A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
arxiv-2210-02406.creator: Tushar Khot, Harsh Trivedi, Matthew Finlayson, Yao Fu, Kyle Richardson, Peter Clark, Ashish Sabharwal
arxiv-2210-02406.description: Abstract Few-shot prompting is a surprisingly powerful way to use Large Language Models (LLMs) to solve various tasks. However, this approach struggles as the task complexity increases or when the individual reasoning steps of the task themselves are hard to learn, especially when embedded in more complex tasks.

arxiv-2212-14708.title: Continuous relay fusion frame in Hilbert spaces
arxiv-2212-14708.creator: Fakhr-dine Nhari 1 and Mohamed Rossafi 2∗
arxiv-2212-14708.description: Abstract . In this paper we introduced the concept of continuous relay fusion frames in Hilbert spaces. And we define the dual frames for continuous relay fusion frames. Finally we study the perturbation probleme of continuous relay fusion frames. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 41A58; Secondary 42C15. 1.

arxiv-2308-03502.title: S. D. Roscani
arxiv-2308-03502.description: Abstract On a Space Fractional Stefan problem of Dirichlet type with Caputo flux Abstract: We study a space-fractional Stefan problem with the Dirichlet boundary conditions. It is a model that describes superdiffusive phenomena. Our main result is the existence of the unique classical solution to this problem.

arxiv-2503-03675.title: The M ∗ − M BH M_{*}-M_{\rm BH} Relation Evolution from z ∼ \sim 6 to the Present Epoch Facilities: JWST
arxiv-2503-03675.creator: Yang Sun, George H. Rieke, Jianwei Lyu (吕建伟), Meredith A. Stone, Zhiyuan Ji, Pierluigi Rinaldi, Christopher N. A. Willmer, Yongda Zhu
arxiv-2503-03675.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yang Sun, George H. Rieke, Jianwei Lyu (吕建伟), Meredith A. Stone, Zhiyuan Ji, Pierluigi Rinaldi, Christopher N. A. Willmer, Yongda Zhu. The ratio between the stellar mass of a galaxy, M ∗ M_{*} , and that of its central supermassive black hole (SMBH), M ∙ M_{\bullet} , the “Magorrian” relationship, traces their coevolution. JWST observations have suggested significant evolution in M ∙ / M ∗ M_{\bullet}/M_{*} relative to local scaling relationships both in low-mass galaxies and in quasars at z ≥ \geq 4.

arxiv-2505-13980.title: Symbolic and Numerical Tools for L ∞ L_{\infty} -Norm Calculation
arxiv-2505-13980.creator: Grace Younes, Alban Quadrat, Fabrice Rouillier
arxiv-2505-13980.description: Abstract The computation of the L ∞ L_{\infty} -norm is an important issue in H ∞ H_{\infty} control, particularly for analyzing system stability and robustness. This paper focuses on symbolic computation methods for determining the L ∞ L_{\infty} -norm of finite-dimensional linear systems, highlighting their advantages in achieving exact solutions where numerical methods often encounter limitations.

arxiv-2506-09399.title: Improving Out-of-Distribution Detection via Dynamic Covariance Calibration
arxiv-2506-09399.creator: Kaiyu Guo, Zijian Wang, Tan Pan, Brian C. Lovell, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh
arxiv-2506-09399.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kaiyu Guo, Zijian Wang, Tan Pan, Brian C. Lovell, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh. Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection is essential for the trustworthiness of AI systems. Methods using prior information (i.e., subspace-based methods) have shown effective performance by extracting information geometry to detect OOD data with a more appropriate distance metric. However, these methods fail to address the geometry distorted by ill-distributed samples, due to the limitation of statically extracting information geometry from the training distribution.

arxiv-2512-24388.title: A closer look at the young stellar group around Sh 2-295
arxiv-2512-24388.creator: J. V. Corrêa-Rodrigues, J. Gregorio-Hetem
arxiv-2512-24388.description: Abstract Context. Star formation is governed by multiple physical processes, making it inherently complicated. One excellent example is the Canis Major OB1/R1 Association, whose complex history of star formation is related to different episodes. Three supernova (SN) events potentially altered the environment and impacted star formation and stellar evolution. Aims.

arxiv-2601-16096.title: Neural Particle Automata: Learning Self-Organizing Particle Dynamics
arxiv-2601-16096.creator: Hyunsoo Kim, Ehsan Pajouheshgar, Sabine Süsstrunk, Wenzel Jakob, Jinah Park
arxiv-2601-16096.description: Abstract . We introduce Neural Particle Automata (NPA), a Lagrangian generalization of Neural Cellular Automata (NCA) from static lattices to dynamic particle systems. Unlike classical Eulerian NCA where cells are pinned to pixels or voxels, NPA model each cell as a particle with a continuous position and internal state, both updated by a shared, learnable neural rule.

pmc-11606956.title: Density-wave-like gap evolution in La3Ni2O7 under high pressure revealed by ultrafast optical spectroscopy
pmc-11606956.creator: Yanghao Meng, Yi Yang, Hualei Sun, Sasa Zhang, Jianlin Luo, Liucheng Chen, Xiaoli Ma, Meng Wang, Fang Hong, Xinbo Wang, Xiaohui Yu
pmc-11606956.description: Density wave (DW) order is believed to be correlated with superconductivity in the recently discovered high-temperature superconductor La3Ni2O7. However, experimental investigations of its evolution under high pressure are still lacking. Here, we explore the quasiparticle dynamics in bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7 single crystals using ultrafast optical pump-probe spectroscopy under high pressures up to 34.2 GPa.

pmc-11867959.description: This study evaluated the impact of meat-processing environmental bacteria (MPB) on biofilm formation by Escherichia coli O157:H7 in dual-species cultures. Biofilm development by 50 MPB and E. coli O157:H7 was assessed using crystal violet staining. Four MPB and E. coli O157:H7 combinations were evaluated further for viable cell numbers.

pmc-12727687.creator: Jeremy F Magland, Ryan Ly, Oliver Rübel, Benjamin Dichter
pmc-12727687.description: The DANDI Archive is a key resource for sharing open neurophysiology data, hosting over 400 datasets in the Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) format. pmc-13003748.title: Long-term clinical remission in rapidly recurrent maxillary osteosarcoma treated with anlotinib-based multimodal therapy: a case report
pmc-13003748.creator: Xinru Wang, Jing Wang, Shuping Li
pmc-13003748.description: BackgroundOsteosarcoma of the jaw is a rare clinical entity characterized by a high propensity for local recurrence, for which surgical resection serves as the primary treatment modality. However, achieving negative margins in the maxilla is often complicated by the proximity of critical neurovascular and orbital structures.

pmc-13265618.title: Editorial: Disambiguating pubertal status from pubertal timing during adolescence: A renewed call for improved construct definition and measurement
pmc-13265618.creator: Kelly L. Klump, Alaina M. Di Dio, Kristen M. Culbert
pmc-13265618.description: There have been numerous past calls for studies to examine pubertal development, rather than just age, in developmental research. These calls are timely and appropriate given the significant effects of pubertal development on a range of internalizing (e.g., eating disorders, depression) and externalizing (e.g., antisocial behavior) disorders.

pmc-13271277.title: Optimizing strategies in tendon tissue engineering through effective scaffold design: overview of recent advancements
pmc-13271277.creator: Gabrielle Lynn Hamner, Justin Lee Brown
pmc-13271277.description: Tendon injuries pose a significant global health challenge due to the poor innate healing capacity of the tissue. Current clinical interventions report limited treatment efficacy, typically resulting in a fibrotic scar that is mechanically inferior to native tissue and predisposed to future re-rupture.

pmc-13314547.title: Identification of Complex Chromosomal Rearrangement Involving Chromosomes 10, 18, and 19 in a Family Undergoing Prenatal Diagnosis: Case Report

pmc-13314547.description: Complex chromosomal rearrangements (CCRs) are rare chromosomal structural abnormalities that are often difficult to be detected. Chromosome conformation‐based karyotyping (c‐Moka) is an emerging technology designed to analyze the three‐dimensional structure of chromosomes, thereby identifying various types of chromosomal structural variations.

pmc-13344924.title: A Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine-based Collision Prediction System with an Angle Optimization Algorithm for Electron Beam Therapy
pmc-13344924.creator: Hideharu Miura, Toshiya Okazue
pmc-13344924.description: Purpose:The purpose of this study was to develop and validate a Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM)-based collision prediction system for electron beam therapy. This system enables a quantitative pretreatment assessment of mechanical interference between the electron applicator and the patient’s body surface. It also automatically proposes safe alternative beam angle combinations.

pmc-13507224.title: Modulation of grape must vitamin content by oenological treatments affects Saccharomyces cerevisiae fermentation performance and wine volatile composition
pmc-13507224.creator: Fabien Garces, Jonathan Picart, Matteo Bosaro, Emilie Riviere, Christophe Morge, Hervé Alexandre, Chloé Roullier-Gall
pmc-13507224.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study explores the impact of oenological treatments with fining agents or yeast-based nutrients on the vitamin content of grape musts, and thus on the fermentative performance of Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeasts and the volatile composition of wine. Products such as bentonites and oenological carbons were shown to deplete several B-group vitamins from the must, while yeast derivatives were able to release significant amounts.
